title: Ukrainian Missile Strike Hits Belgorod Logistics Hub and Power Plant, Killing 2
detail: A Ukrainian missile strike hit the Russian city of Belgorod on August 30, striking a logistics facility housing an Ozon sorting center and delivery hub, setting seven warehouses ablaze. Acting regional Governor Alexander Shuvaev said the strike killed 2 people — a man and a 16-year-old — and injured 16 others. OSINT channels and Ukrainska Pravda also reported damage to the Belgorod thermal power plant, where a fire broke out, and strikes near a television tower. Ozon confirmed its facility was hit and said it evacuated employees before the strike. Kyiv officials have accused both Ozon and its rival Wildberries of supplying components and logistics support to the Russian military, and Ukraine has struck Wildberries warehouses in Tambov, Kotovsk, and Moscow Oblast in preceding weeks as part of the same campaign.

media.caption: Fire at the Ozon logistics facility in Belgorod following the Aug. 30 Ukrainian strike

title: Ukraine Strikes Russia's Kirishi Oil Refinery and Yeysk Airfield in Overnight Raid
detail: Ukraine's defense forces struck the KINEF oil refinery in Kirishi, Leningrad Oblast — Russia's second-largest refinery by capacity at roughly 20 million tonnes of crude processed annually — during the night of August 29-30, igniting a fire in the plant's industrial zone. Leningrad Governor Alexander Drozdenko said regional air defenses intercepted 42 drones overnight. In the same operational window, Ukrainian forces also struck the Yeysk military airfield in Krasnodar Krai and a drone launch and storage facility in Millerovo, Rostov Oblast, with fires confirmed at both sites. The Kirishi strike extends Ukraine's 2026 campaign against Russian refining capacity, which has already hit facilities in Yaroslavl, Ryazan, Saratov, Salavat, Nizhnekamsk, and Krasnodar Krai this year.

media.caption: Fire reported at the Kirishi (KINEF) oil refinery, Leningrad Oblast, after an overnight Ukrainian drone strike

title: Death Toll From Kyiv-Area Ammunition Depot Strike Rises to 38 as Russia Vows 'Massive' Energy Strikes
detail: The confirmed death toll from the August 28 Russian drone strike on an ammunition storage facility in Myla, Kyiv Oblast, rose to 38 killed by August 30, with 4 people still missing, President Zelensky said — making it one of the deadliest single strikes of 2026. The blast damaged roughly 50 buildings and forced the evacuation of more than 380 residents; among the dead was the mayor of nearby Dmytrivka. The same day, Russia's Defense Ministry announced via Telegram that it had begun preparing 'massive strikes' against Ukraine's energy infrastructure, framing the move as retaliation for Ukraine's continuing deep-strike campaign against Russian civilian and energy facilities. The warning revived fears of a repeat of prior winters, when sustained Russian bombardment of Ukraine's power grid left millions without heat and electricity. Bloomberg reported Moscow is escalating because it views peace negotiations as stalled, with sources citing possible intensified conventional ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv and other cities. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called Russia's posture 'tough' but said 'military escalation is simply not necessary for Moscow ... because we're advancing anyway.'

media.caption: Russia's Sarmat intercontinental ballistic missile, illustrating coverage of Moscow's Aug. 30 warning of 'massive strikes' on Ukraine's energy grid
